reason: The ceiling arithmetic works (450 FP x 6.6e-6 = 0.0030, plus 400 FN x 7.4e-6 = 0.0030, plus a node term of 0.0007, gives about 0.0067), but its premise is wrong. Marginals, micro-averaged with D = TP+FP+FN = 135,729: turning an FN into a TP is worth 1/D = 7.4e-6, and removing an FP is worth TP/D^2 = 6.6e-6. These check against the measured stitch result (281 TP and 19 FP predicted +0.00195, measured +0.00197). Embryo weights, taken from the b_break oracle (41 FN -> +0.00198 on 44b6, 358 FN -> +0.00317 on 6bba): 44b6 D is about 20.7k (15%) and 6bba about 113k (85%). (1) The FN half of the ceiling is not reachable. The correction says swap and diverted FNs are node-POSITION errors between two tracks. The GT-oracle survivor simulation changed TP by -2 (6bba sample), so the only gain is FP removal: 6bba FP went from 1247 to 1209 in 25 videos, about 300 FP over 199 videos (about 0.002). (2) Measured GT-oracle ceiling: +0.0004 on 44b6 and +0.0020 on 6bba. Weighted, that is +0.0017 in edges, plus at most +0.0008 from the node term, so about +0.0025 at best. That is 2.7x below the claimed +0.007. The oracle itself fails the protocol: the overall gain is under the +0.002 gate, and 44b6 at +0.0004 is under the +0.001 per-embryo gate. (3) The head-gated arm only merges pairs whose refined positions converge under 2.0 um. With head shifts of mean 0.74 and max 1.61 um, and raw pairs no closer than about 3.25 um, the merges fall almost entirely in the <4 um band. The oracle there is -0.0003 (44b6) / +0.0001 (6bba), about +0.00004 weighted. (4) Node term: each deleted node is worth 0.00092/41.3k = 2.2e-8, about 0.3% of one edge. R<4 deletes 0.15-0.2% of nodes, so at most +0.00015. (5) Break-even precision on merges that touch evaluable edges is about 7.4/(7.4+6.6) = 53%. The edges touching pairs are 1,350 TP against 455 FP (a 25% FP share), and every head-free rule measured below 50% (-0.002 to -0.013). (6) Division term: losing one division TP (23/194 -> 22/195) costs 0.1 x 0.0058 = -0.00058, which alone cancels the whole realistic gain. The 'exclude forks and the 2 frames after' guard cannot be applied at the pre-relink insertion point, because safe-division and DaughterNet forks are created after relink; sisters 3-6 um apart are exactly the pairs a head could converge. Realistic fraction captured: about 0-10% of the recomputed +0.0025 ceiling, i.e. +0.0000 to +0.0002. That is below public-LB resolution and about 1% of the +0.022 needed to reach 0.97.
fix_if_any: Nothing makes it clear the gate. The best repair is to turn it into a free CPU diagnostic on the x138 head capture once that exists: count the raw <5 um pairs whose refined positions converge under 2.0/2.5 um, per embryo and per distance band. Kill it if fewer than 100 GT-involved converged pairs fall in the 4-5 um band (the only band with oracle value). If it survives, apply it as a pre-relink merge that is vetoed for any pair where either member is a safe-division or DaughterNet daughter candidate (run the safe-div candidate test first) or where the pair diverges by t+2. Ship it only as a zero-cost bundle component with CI > 0 and both embryos >= 0, never as a standalone probe. The GPU and LB budget is better spent on retraining/extending the coordinate head and on detection recall (1,907 FN with no node within 7 um, about +0.014 at 7.4e-6 each), which targets the same swap-zone position errors directly.
realistic_public_gain: +0.0000 to +0.0002 (head-gated, <4 um band); hard ceiling about +0.0025 even with a GT-oracle survivor; one lost division TP (-0.0006) can make it negative. Not resolvable on the public LB.
